hypotheses.justification: The conclusion holds even when q = 0. For any nonzero level M, use deg_eq_one_modularFunctionFieldBar as in the original proof. At level 0, the definitions of divisorExpansions, modularFunctionFieldFull and laurentBaseChange show that modularFunctionFieldBar 0 is generated by the coefficient-embedded qExpand ℚ d jq for all nonzero d. Each generator is algebraic over the field generated by the embedded jq, by B2Deg.finiteDimensional_adjoin_jBar d in S_ModularCurve_deg_eq_one_modularFunctionFieldBar.lean. IntermediateField.isAlgebraic_adjoin therefore makes the whole extension algebraic. B2Deg.deg_eq_one_of_isAlgebraic_adjoin then gives degree one for every place at level 0 too. The original degree subtraction finishes. Thus primality is unnecessary; both reported hypotheses can also be removed together.

The field and divisor expressions in the statement do not require this instance. Removing it additionally permits N = 0. At level 0, modularFunctionFieldBar is generated by the embedded qExpand ℚ d jq for nonzero d; B2Deg.finiteDimensional_adjoin_jBar d makes each algebraic over the field generated by the embedded jq. IntermediateField.isAlgebraic_adjoin and B2Deg.deg_eq_one_of_isAlgebraic_adjoin give degree one for every place, including at this level. At nonzero levels, deg_eq_one_modularFunctionFieldBar applies directly. In either case, Divisor.degree_single and map_sub give degree 1 - 1 = 0. Both reported hypotheses can be removed together.
